<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **3** package(s): `@objectstack/objectql`, `@objectstack/plugin-security`, `@objectstack/verify`, touching **27** documentable anchor(s).

**28** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 41dc302496e48ed23d3dcd23f61d6365448237eb`.

⛔ **10** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `ObjectQL (symbol, 80 pages)`, `master_detail (literal, 40 pages)`
- **3** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **63** of **222** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **159** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **159**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **104** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **35** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 41dc302496e48ed23d3dcd23f61d6365448237eb` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `2d0679ec7a3daca64392b24c900f5ab7794866bb` — the merge of head `67209e8962ffb3c614fca22a37997becad76d1e6` into base `41dc302496e48ed23d3dcd23f61d6365448237eb`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 2d0679ec7a3daca64392b24c900f5ab7794866bb && git checkout 2d0679ec7a3daca64392b24c900f5ab7794866bb
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 41dc302496e48ed23d3dcd23f61d6365448237eb 67209e8962ffb3c614fca22a37997becad76d1e6 && git checkout -B drift-repro 41dc302496e48ed23d3dcd23f61d6365448237eb && git merge --no-ff 67209e8962ffb3c614fca22a37997becad76d1e6

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 41dc302496e48ed23d3dcd23f61d6365448237eb
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 41dc302496e48ed23d3dcd23f61d6365448237eb` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

Contract review for card #29029 · narrowing face (`Clause-②: yes (narrowing)`) · read-only reviewer at the contract-review tier, brief per `record-recognisers --template --face narrowing` · 2026-11-06T19:09Z

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `67209e8962ffb3c614fca22a37997becad76d1e6`
Local-runs: none
Scope: every non-prose path of the diff (35 paths: `.changeset/29029-lookup-user-caller-read.md`, `docs/qa/platform-checklist/areas/records-forms.json`, `packages/objectql/src/engine.ts`, `engine-validate.ts`, `engine-referential-integrity.ts`, `engine-references-and-master-detail.ts`, `engine-master-detail-related.ts`, the eight `packages/objectql/src/*.test.ts`, `packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/delegated-admin-gate.ts`, `security-plugin-authz-middleware.ts`, `__tests__/rig-users.testkit.ts`, the thirteen `packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/*.test.ts`, the four `packages/plugins/plugin-audit/src/*.test.ts`, `packages/qa/dogfood/test/predicate-relationship-traversal.dogfood.test.ts`, `packages/verify/src/parent-write-reach.ts`, `parent-write-reach.test.ts`), judged in full for the delta `0e54448624..67209e8962` and leaned on record 6673498665 for the part unchanged since `0e54448624` + packages/objectql/src/engine-top-level.ts (`servedAsStored`), packages/objectql/src/engine-find.ts (`fillQueryAstDefaults`), packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/predicate-guard.ts (`assertReadableQueryFields`), packages/plugins/plugin-security/src/field-masker.ts, content/docs/permissions/system-context.mdx (row 23 and the generated register), content/docs/api/error-catalog.mdx, content/docs/data-modeling/fields.mdx, content/docs/permissions/delegated-administration.mdx

`reviewFace` returns no `hits` on the 40 paths, so the face is the changeset's `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)`. The net diff was read three-dot against `origin/main` at `41dc302496`: 40 files, +1739 / −248, matching the PR's file list. The head's merge base with `origin/main` IS `origin/main`'s tip, so the delta against `main` is exactly the PR's own hunks.

**What moved since the predecessor's PASS (6673498665 at `0e54448624`).** Four merges of `origin/main` and five commits of the seat's own: the forgiveness fix (`engine-referential-integrity.ts`, two host lines in `engine.ts`), its tests (one new plugin-security suite, one new describe in the objectql suite), the changeset and two docs sentences, the system-context row, and three import lines in the verify test. A per-path comparison of the PR's hunks at `0e54448624` against its hunks at this head finds them byte-identical on every other path; where `main` also moved a file (`engine.ts`, `security-plugin-authz-middleware.ts`, `records-forms.json`, `grant-permission-set-name.test.ts`, three docs pages) the PR's lines are unchanged and only the surrounding context differs.

### ① Derived judgments

- **The update's reference forgiveness narrows (BREAKING) — right.** `assertReferencesResolve` still forgives a refused `master_detail`, `lookup` or `user` value that every row the write lands on already stores (#29062), but the rows it compares against are now `storedReferencesCallerReads`: one `find` of those rows through the caller's own door, projected to `id` and the refused columns, and a column kept only where the door served it exactly as stored (`servedAsStored`, the comparison the `update`-mode validate preview already makes). A hidden column (the key deleted), a masked or rewritten one (`servedAsStored` false), an unreturned row (no view) and a failed read (the catch) each keep no column, so they forgive nothing and the value is refused like any other. The refusal is built from the sent value alone, so the answer is the same whatever the column holds — pinned for the three types, by id and in bulk, in both new suites, with the stored rows untouched.
- **Identical answer by id and in bulk — right.** By-id hands `[priorRecord]`, bulk hands the `readPriorRows` memo; both pass through the same projection and the same `every(...)` test. A bulk write whose matched rows the door returns only in part keeps no column for the missing rows, and `every` then refuses — the fail-closed direction.
- **A caller who can read the column keeps the forgiveness — right.** With the column served as stored, the stored id is kept and `storedReferenceIds(...).has(value)` admits the carried-back value; controls pinned under the real security plugin (`readable: true, editable: true`) and under an engine middleware that serves the row whole.
- **System and flow-run writes unchanged — right.** `assertReferencesResolve` returns at once for a system write that is not a flow run's; a flow run's write reaches `storedReferencesCallerReads`, which answers `rows` unchanged on `isSystem`, so it compares as stored, as before; pinned for both doors.
- **The extra read is the caller's door, projected, and fails closed — right.** `this.find(object, { where: { id }, fields: ['id', ...refused], context })` under the caller's own context, so RBAC, RLS, sharing and the field masker all answer it; the engine applies no default `limit` of its own (`fillQueryAstDefaults` fills none); the predicate guard refuses a hidden field only in `where`/`having`/`orderBy`, never in the projection, so the hidden column comes back absent rather than as a refusal — either way it forgives nothing. A thrown read is caught, logged and keeps no column.
- **No double count and no ordering change against the validation rules — right.** The stored-row read runs only after a probe has refused, once per refusing write, inside the same `checkReferences` closure the doors already order by `referencesCheckedBeforeRules`; the rules' `previous` is still the unprojected pre-image, as it was, and the reference check's order against them is untouched on all four doors and the preview.
- **The rest of the accept set (6673498665).** `lookup` and `user` on the caller's read door, `tree` on the elevated probe, the sys_user ban asked only for a readable user, the delegate's `sys_business_unit` read admitted only on refusal, only for the read verbs, only on the caller's own behalf and only as a non-empty `id IN` — re-read in the tree at this head and unchanged.
- **Public surface.** `storedReferencesCallerReads` is a module export of a file the package does not re-export, and the host's `find` is a private `this` type; no `packages/spec` path, no authorable key, no emitted declaration moves. `@objectstack/plugin-security`'s additive methods are as recorded on 6673498665.

### ② Semver level

- Changeset `.changeset/29029-lookup-user-caller-read.md`: `@objectstack/objectql`, `@objectstack/plugin-security`, `@objectstack/verify` at **patch**, with the BREAKING banner, the ADR-0087 disposition (`not-required (no-migration-prescription)`), and the upgrade sentence. The amendment adds the forgiveness paragraph, which states exactly what the tree does: by id and in bulk, a column the caller may edit but not read judges every value as new, a readable column keeps the forgiveness, a system write is unchanged. Right.
- `Clause-②: yes (narrowing)` is line-initial in both the PR body and the changeset and now names the forgiveness narrowing in the same sentence as the reference-check narrowing; `Metadata-protocol: none` stands, because what narrows is runtime data writes and no authorable key changes. The title is `fix(objectql)!`. Right.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Must `main` be merged again?** Not at this head: `67209e8962` merges `origin/main` at `41dc302496`, which is `origin/main`'s tip at read time, so the head is a descendant of `main` and the three-dot diff is the PR alone. All four merges on the branch (`5b7d00f22b`, `8e127e3c0b`, `dc1dbb4db7`, `67209e8962`) produce exactly the tree `git merge-tree` produces from their parents — no hand resolution — and the per-path comparison above shows no PR hunk altered by any of them. The owed merge before queueing is a sequence item for the seat only if `main` moves again.
- **Edits beyond the fix, each answered.** `parent-write-reach.test.ts`: two side-effect imports of packages the harness already loads lazily, paid at collection for `check:test-source-alias`'s source-reach rule; no assertion changes. `system-context.mdx` row 23: states that an update's check does not judge again a value every landed row stores, that a system write compares those rows as stored and every other write only as the caller may read them — true of the tree — and its Symbol cell and the register gain `storedReferencesCallerReads` at count 1, which is the function's one `isSystem` read. `error-catalog.mdx` and `fields.mdx`: one sentence each, matching the code. The changeset amendment: see ②.
- **Check-runs at read time** (53 on the head): 33 success, 14 skipped, 5 in progress (`Test Core` shards 1, 2, 3, 4, 6), 1 failure. The failure is `PR-body guards`, whose duplicate-claim leg refuses because #30747 still declares a fix for #29029; it re-runs on `edited`/`synchronize` and clears once the seat closes #30747 with its pointer, as the PR body already announces. Every Type Check, Lint, Build and Governed Surface Queue Guard run has completed green. The pending shards and the retirement of #30747 stay owed before the queue; neither is a finding against the tree.
- **Landing constraints, not findings:** the maintainer's per-PR BREAKING word (6676395836) was given on #30747 for this change on condition of security#1's clear, a `main` merge and green CI; this PR is the security seat's own continuation, carries the same rule plus the forgiveness narrowing, and the changeset and body name the addition. Whether that word carries to the superseding PR is the maintainer's to say, not this record's.

### ④ Design judgment

**The narrowing, read against the published spec on `main`.** The spec's `reference_not_found` says a reference the caller cannot read answers as one that exists nowhere. On `main` the forgiveness contradicted that for an editable, unreadable column: whether an update landed depended on the stored value of a column the caller may not read. The fix makes the spec's own refusal real there — a value named in such a column is judged on its own, and the write's answer no longer carries anything about what the column holds — and takes away no declared capability at the consumer: a readable column, a system write and a flow run's write behave as documented.

**Attempts to break it**, each read in the tree at the head:
- **A path that still compares against an unprojected pre-image inside the reference check:** none. Both `storedRows` suppliers (by-id, bulk) reach the same projection; the insert and preview doors hand no stored rows; the `update`-mode preview runs no reference check at all (pre-existing, below).
- **A readable caller wrongly refused:** a lookup served as its id (no `expand` in the projection, no file field, no formula) compares `Object.is`-equal to the stored id; a `Date`, array or plain-object value compares structurally. A caller who can read the row but not the column is refused by design. A caller whose read door returns the row only partially (RLS drops some matched rows of a bulk write) loses the forgiveness for the whole batch — fail-closed, and the change the rule asks for.
- **Performance cliff:** one `find` per refusing write, never per row, and only after a probe has refused; the pre-image read it compares against was already paid. The per-value caller read (`callerReadableReferenceExists`) is as recorded on 6673498665.
- **System-write exemption, flow-run order, `tree`, the sys_user ban composition, the delegate read:** unchanged since `0e54448624`, re-read.

**Findings: none must-fix.** Should-fix, none blocking this PR:
1. The by-id update's repoint detection (read only when the detail declares a parent-scoped `requiredWhen`) still takes the stored header id from the stored row rather than from the caller's view. It should follow the same rule as this PR. Pre-existing and outside this card's surface → carried by the security seat.
2. The `update`-mode validate preview still runs no reference check (6673498665 item 5). Unchanged. → engine lane.
3. The forgiveness read sets no page bound of its own; a driver or middleware page cap on `find` would drop matched rows beyond it and refuse the batch (fail-closed). → note on the engine lane, with the preview's read sharing the shape.
4. Items 1–4 and 6 of 6673498665 stand as recorded there.
